messages:
Support Jen: Hey team — ACME (tenant acme-corp) opened a support case: sudden 429s and latency spikes since ~09:10 UTC. They report requests that should hit their dedicated 'gold' pool are getting routed to shared pools and then throttled. Logs show 429 + pool=shared-1. Can we triage?

Ashwin: Thanks Jen. Do we have the routing decision logs + request headers? Any recent control-plane deploys rolled out to eu-west-1?

Support Jen: Pasted the minimal repro from ACME (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Redwood-Tier: gold
X-Tenant-ID: acme-corp
Content-Type: application/json
{ "input": "hello" }
```
Response: 429 {"error":"rate_limited","pool":"shared-1"} - started 2024-11-06T09:09:58Z

Clare: Hmm. We recently merged a change to tier header parsing to support arrays (https://github.com/redwood/controlplane/pull/482). Could be a casing/trim bug. Can somebody dump the route-eval debug for that tenant?

SRE Oncall: I pulled the decision trace for a sample request (from the agent logs):
```
route_eval: request.headers["x-redwood-tier"] -> [" \"gold\" "]
normalize_tiers() -> ["\"gold\""]
policy_match("gold") -> false
fallback_policy() -> select shared-1
```
That looks like the parser left surrounding quotes. :grimacing:

Ashwin: That explains it. The extra quotes mean the string didn't match the canonical tier key "gold" so the policy fell through. Sounds like a control-plane string-trimming regression. Which deploy included that change?

Clare: The change was rolled 2024-11-06 08:45 UTC as part of controlplane v3.14.2 (canary -> prod). I'm seeing a spike in similar warnings in the controlplane logs: `WARN: tier_parser: unexpected token '"'` starting ~08:46.

InfraBot: Alert: controlplane v3.14.2 deployed to eu-west-1 at 2024-11-06T08:45:12Z; 120k route evaluations since deploy; error rate for tier parsing +match failure increased by 18%.

Support Jen: Customer wants an ETA and a workaround. Can we quickly mitigate? They are on Dedicated with strict SLA.

SRE Oncall: Short term mitigation: add a tenant-level override to pin acme-corp to their gold pool. CLI to apply: 
```
redwoodctl routing override create --tenant acme-corp --pool gold-dedicated-01 --reason "hotfix: tier parser regression"
```
This will avoid evaluation until we roll back/fix. I can apply now if owners OK.

Clare: +1 from me. Also recommend a quick rollback of controlplane to v3.14.1 in eu-west-1 canary to validate fix before full rollback. If rollback shows no regressions we can promote.

Ashwin: I'll own the fix PR to trim quotes and add unit coverage. Plan: revert naive array-string concat behavior, add canonicalization step (strip quotes + whitespace), add a regression test for headers with both single string and JSON array forms. Target PR and canary rebuild in next 90 minutes.

Support Jen: I told ACME we'll apply tenant override now and provide follow-up within 2 hours. Applying override, will update with confirmation once in effect.

SRE Oncall: Override applied at 09:18 UTC. Verified traffic to acme-corp now hits gold-dedicated-01; 429s stopped for their requests in the next 2 minutes sample.

Support Jen: Customer confirmed lower latency and no more 429s. They asked for post-mortem and whether they'll be billed for throttled requests. Finance: treat as credit — we should waive the throttled token usage for this incident.

Clare: Filing a postmortem doc and linking to PR once merged. Action items: (1) Ashwin PR to fix parser + tests, (2) rollback validation or patch release, (3) add automated E2E that exercises header variants, (4) billing credit to ACME.

Ashwin: Working on PR now (draft up). Will ping when ready for review.

SRE Oncall: Adding follow-up monitoring: assert route_eval mismatches <0.1% in next 24h, alert on spike.

Support Jen: Thanks all — closing the support loop with ACME and will attach steps + override ID. :white_check_mark:
